newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Briton, Canadian win Nobel Economics prize.
newsitem.headline: Briton, Canadian win Nobel Economics prize.

text.p: British professor James Mirrlees and Canadian William Vickrey won the 1996 Nobel Economics Prize, the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences said on Tuesday.
The academy said the $1.12 million prize was awarded for "their fundamental contributions to the economic theory of incentives under assymetric information."
Mirrlees was born in Minnigaff, Scotland in 1936 and is now teaching economics at the University of Cambridge, in England.
Vickrey was born in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada, in 1914 and is now Professor Emeritus at Columbia University, New York, where he also served as a tax advisor between 1937 and 1947.

The economics prize is known formally as The Bank of Sweden Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel and is the youngest of the prestigious awards, having been given for the first time in 1968.
The academy said Vickrey's research concerned the properties of different types of auctions and how they can be best designed to generate economic efficiency.
Mirrlees, 25 years later, capitalised on Vickrey's work in relation to work with taxation.
